summary: Tioga County, PA state fire tower of steel Blaw-Knox design, built 1922-23 and removed in 1973; no source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1973; no source describes the site now.

events.note: Wellsboro Gazette reports the State Department of Forestry erecting the tower on Rarick hill (October 1922), and calls it new in December 1922
Register gives 1923 for the steel Blaw-Knox tower; an April 1923 Wellsboro Agitator item still describes the work as about to start
Towerman John Badman on duty at the tower
Fire at the D.M. Clemons house at Crooked Creek, seen from the tower; the house burned
Frank Starkey named as towerman on the Rarick tower in an April 1949 Wellsboro Gazette list of five Tioga County towers
Register and Forest Lookouts page both record the tower removed in 1973
Registered September 16, 2008 as FFLOS US 437, PA 266

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1923. The Wellsboro Gazette reported the tower being erected in October 1922 and called it new in December 1922, while an April 1923 Wellsboro Agitator item still described the work as about to start. The story reports the sources without choosing one.

notes_for_editor: The newspaper quotes come from a hobby site's transcriptions; the Wellsboro Gazette and Agitator originals were not read. The 1922 and 1923 build dates conflict; the story gives both. No source describes the site now, and access is unknown. A search result (Facebook, July 2026) concerns a 1922 Blaw-Knox tower from Sideling Hill, Fulton County, restored at the Pennsylvania Lumber Museum; it is a different tower and was not used. The record's coordinates (41.8473, -77.1569) were not checked against a source. Web searches used: 2. Pages read: the Forest Lookouts page, the register page, and cached pages.
